open_points.subject: failure path representation
open_points.question: What exact data shape and syntax represents a failure path in an operation's answer?
options: A sequence of typed components, such as ["picks",1,"alias"]
A structured object with separate input, position, field, record-kind and id members
open_points.default_guess: Use a sequence of string names and integer list positions.

witness.initial: A correction request contains an alias longer than 40 characters in the second item of a list input.
events: The operation reports the stage-(4) alias failure with the required path.
outcomes: One implementation returns the path as ["picks",1,"alias"].
Another implementation returns the path as "picks[1].alias".
witness.observer: The caller and any owner-interface renderer or contract test consuming the error answer

open_points.subject: record failure path
open_points.text: a record by its kind and its id or position
open_points.question: When a failing record has both a readable id and a position in an input list, must its path use the id, the position, or both?
options: Use the id whenever it is readable, otherwise the position
Include both the id and the position
open_points.default_guess: Use the id when readable and the position only when no readable id exists.

witness.initial: An uploaded import contains a picked project's malformed second room, and that room has a readable room id.
events: The owner asks for the import mapping.
The mapping reports the malformed-room entry.
outcomes: One implementation names the room by its room id.
Another implementation names the room by its position in the project's room list.
witness.observer: The owner viewing the mapping and tests comparing its error paths

open_points.subject: list positions in failure paths
open_points.text: such as the alias of the second pick
open_points.question: What numeric list position represents the second item: 1 or 2?
options: Zero-based positions, so the second item is 1
One-based positions, so the second item is 2

witness.initial: The second pick has an alias longer than 40 characters.
events: The owner requests the import mapping.
The mapping names the failing alias by a path containing its list position.
witness.observer: The owner, API clients and exact contract tests

open_points.subject: ordering failure paths with unlike components
open_points.text: a name by Unicode code point, a list position as a number, a shorter path first
open_points.question: How are two paths ordered when the first unequal components are of different kinds, one a name and the other a numeric list position?
options: Such paths must first be normalised so unlike component kinds never occur at the same depth

witness.initial: A picked project has two malformed rooms reported under the same error kind: one has readable id "z" and an invalid instant, while the other has no readable id and is identified by its list position.
events: The owner asks for the import mapping.
The implementation constructs one record path using the readable id and the other using the position.
It sorts both entries within the same error kind.
outcomes: An implementation that orders names first reports the room identified by "z" first.
An implementation that orders positions first reports the room identified by its numeric position first.
witness.observer: The owner viewing the mapping and tests comparing the ordered failures

open_points.subject: periodic-pass deadline after a call
open_points.text: waits for the first deadline at or after it
open_points.question: If the reading taken when a call returns is exactly the deadline that caused that call, is that deadline already consumed, or does it cause another immediate call?
options: The triggering deadline is consumed; wait for the next strictly later deadline
Select the equal deadline again and make another call immediately
Track the last consumed deadline explicitly and select the first deadline later than it and not earlier than the reading
open_points.default_guess: Treat every triggering deadline as consumed and wait for the first unconsumed deadline strictly after it.

witness.initial: Serving began at monotonic reading 0, the interval is 60 seconds, and a pass call due at 60 returns quickly enough that the next monotonic reading is still exactly 60.
events: instance_lifecycle makes the call due at 60.
The pass takes its required reading and obtains 60.
outcomes: An implementation that consumes the triggering deadline waits until 120 for the next call.
A literal at-or-after implementation selects 60 again and immediately calls again, potentially repeating while the clock reading remains 60.
witness.observer: Callers of the process, who see normal service in the first implementation and timer-loop starvation or extra pass calls in the second
